metadata.summary: Jake Paul has confirmed kickboxing champion Cedric Doumbe as his opponent for his return to the boxing ring in Dubai on Christmas Eve.
metadata.content: Jake Paul to fight kickboxing champion Cedric Doumbe on Christmas Eve as YouTuber's opponent is revealed | Boxing News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Breaking Jake Paul to fight kickboxing champion Cedric Doumbe on Christmas Eve as YouTuber's opponent is revealed Jake Paul will make his boxing return on Christmas Eve in Dubai, 12 months on from having his jaw broken by Anthony Joshua; former two-time world champion kickboxer turned MMA fighter Cedric Doumbe confirmed as his opponent Monday 2 November 2026 12:00, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch Jake Paul’s new opponent, Cedric Doumbe, leave Kylian Mbappe stunned with this nine-second knockout in the PFL Jake Paul has confirmed kickboxing champion Cedric Doumbe as his opponent for his return to the boxing ring in Dubai on Christmas Eve. It's Paul's first fight since he took on former two-time unified heavyweight world champion Anthony Joshua, where he suffered a broken jaw from a sixth-round knockout blow. Back in 2024, the YouTuber turned boxer also fought a then-58-year-old Mike Tyson and has a record of 12-2, with seven KOs, since making his professional debut. messages.text: Boulter wins in Hong Kong after incident 'got under my skin'

metadata.summary: Katie Boulter battled into the second round of the Hong Kong Open with a straight-sets victory over Viktorija Golubic, despite an incident that "got under my skin", according to the British No 1.
metadata.content: Katie Boulter wins in Hong Kong despite incident that 'got under my skin' during match versus Viktorija Golubic | Tennis News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Katie Boulter wins in Hong Kong despite incident that 'got under my skin' during match versus Viktorija Golubic Katie Boulter was twice broken when serving for the match in the second set after British No 1 says incident "got under my skin"; the world No 49 went on to beat Viktorija Golubic 6-2 7-6; watch the ATP Paris Masters live on Sky Sports from Monday November 2 Monday 2 November 2026 11:56, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Katie Boulter questions the umpire’s call over outside noise and said that it ‘got under my skin’ in her interview after beating Viktorija Golubic. Katie Boulter battled into the second round of the Hong Kong Open with a straight-sets victory over Viktorija Golubic, despite an incident that "got under my skin", according to the British No 1. Boulter was twice broken when serving for the match in the second set, having complained to the umpire when up 5-2 after a point was not replayed despite her being distracted by a noise from outside the court. She ultimately triumphed in a tiebreak to take the match 6-2 7-6 (7-2), clinching a fourth win in five following on from reaching the semi-finals in Japan Open last month that saw her reclaim top spot from Sonay Kartal as British No 1. messages.text: Haskell backs Borthwick, Pollock as England prepare for Nations Championship

metadata.summary: James Haskell has backed Steve Borthwick as "the right man for the job" as England prepare for the conclusion of the inaugural Nations Championship in November.
metadata.content: England Rugby: Steve Borthwick and Henry Pollock backed by James Haskell ahead of Nations Championship fixtures | Rugby Union News | Sky Sports Skip to main content England Rugby: Steve Borthwick and Henry Pollock backed by James Haskell ahead of Nations Championship fixtures James Haskell believes Steve Borthwick is the right man to lead England at the 2027 Rugby World Cup and shares his excitement over rising star Henry Pollock ahead of November's Nations Championship fixtures against Australia, Japan and New Zealand at Allianz Stadium, Twickenham By Matthew Wolfe Monday 2 November 2026 06:01, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player England head coach Steve Borthwick says that contract extension hasn't changed the focus on 2027 World Cup James Haskell has backed Steve Borthwick as "the right man for the job" as England prepare for the conclusion of the inaugural Nations Championship in November. Borthwick oversaw England's worst-ever Six Nations campaign earlier this year, with four losses from their five matches, but despite growing pressure the RFU have publicly expressed their support for Borthwick through to the 2027 Rugby World Cup in Australia. This month, England will face Australia, Japan and New Zealand ahead of Finals Weekend, which takes place November 27-28 at Twickenham. Former England international Haskell, who earned 77 Test caps between 2007 and 2019, insists it is not the time to change the head coach. Nations Championship: Schedule

This is how it was meant to be. When Mercedes announced in August 2024 that they were fast-tracking Kimi Antonelli - who had turned 18 just days earlier - into one of Formula 1's most desirable seats, expectations could not have been set much higher. Fast-forward a little more than two years, and the Italian has delivered on his billing as a generational talent by becoming the sport's youngest world champion at the age of 20 . messages.text: Hamilton hits out at Leclerc after Mexico clash

metadata.summary: Lewis Hamilton criticised Charles Leclerc over the lap-one incident that cost Ferrari likely victory in the Mexico City Grand Prix, suggesting his team-mate's driving came down to "a mentality thing".
metadata.content: Lewis Hamilton hits out at Charles Leclerc after Ferrari drivers' Mexico City GP clash as he questions team-mate's approach | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Lewis Hamilton hits out at Charles Leclerc after Ferrari drivers' Mexico City GP clash as he questions team-mate's approach Ferrari drivers' lap-one squabble effectively lost them the race to Red Bull's Max Verstappen; Hamilton says of Leclerc: "I don't think it's an age thing. I think it's a mentality thing"; watch every session of the Sao Paulo GP from this Friday, live on Sky Sports F1 Monday 2 November 2026 09:12, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lewis Hamilton was left furious after Ferrari team-mate Charles Leclerc overtook him on the opening lap while leaving the track but was only given a five-second penalty for the infringement. Lewis Hamilton criticised Charles Leclerc over the lap-one incident that cost Ferrari likely victory in the Mexico City Grand Prix, suggesting his team-mate's driving came down to "a mentality thing". Hamilton and Leclerc battled for the lead during the first four corners of Sunday's race at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez in a duel that saw the latter cut across the second chicane to take over first place from the pole-sitting Briton. Having also run slightly wide himself in defence of the position, Hamilton was overtaken on the exit of Turn Five by Max Verstappen.
